name: Leica Super-Vario-Elmar-SL 16-35 f/3.5-4.5 ASPH.
notes: Order no. 11177. Leica's press release put the lens on sale from 23 April 2018. Leica lists 18 elements in 12 groups with two aspherical elements and three elements of glass with anomalous partial dispersion, and a close focus distance of 25 cm (used for both ends of the zoom). Non-official values: the launch price of USD 5,495 comes from launch news/retailer coverage (PetaPixel, B&H); the stepping-motor AF, the non-extending (internal) zoom and the floating-element focusing come from B&H's product description; the smallest aperture f/22 (given only as the aperture range, so the tele-end value is left null) also comes from B&H. The 82 mm filter thread is inferred from Leica's own accessory listing (lens cap E82). Weight, dimensions, number of aperture blades and maximum magnification did not appear in any accessible source and are null; whether the lens has optical stabilisation was not stated explicitly in the accessible sources, so stabilization is null. The Lensrentals link is a rental listing, not a review, so it is classed as a retailer source; no independent review is listed for this lens.
famousFor: The widest zoom in Leica's SL line-up, a weather-protected 16-35mm for L-Mount bodies built around an 18-element design with anomalous-dispersion glass for tight control of colour fringing.
strengths: Internal zoom: the barrel does not extend when zooming
Weather-protected build with AquaDura coating on the front element
Fast, quiet autofocus
Close focus of 25 cm across the zoom range
weaknesses: Slower f/3.5-4.5 aperture than f/2.8 ultra-wide zooms
Very expensive for an ultra-wide zoom
Large 82 mm filters needed
bestFor: Landscapes and seascapes in bad weather
Travel and street scenes with a wide perspective

name: Leica Summilux-M 35 f/1.4 ASPH.
notes: This is the current redesign announced by Leica on 15 September 2022 (order no. 11726 black, 11727 silver), which replaced the 2010 FLE version: 11 aperture blades instead of 9, close focus 40 cm instead of 70 cm (via a double-cam mechanism; the range 70-40 cm is outside the rangefinder coupling and is focused with live view or an EVF) and a round integrated lens hood. Leica lists 9 elements in 5 groups with one aspherical element and 'several' elements of anomalous-partial-dispersion glass; the number of those is not published, so only the aspherical element is itemised. The elements behind the aperture form a floating group. maxMagnification is null: the researched ratio of 1:17.4 fits a 35 mm lens focused at the old 0.7 m limit (the 2010 FLE version / end of the rangefinder coupling), not at this version's 0.4 m close focus, where a thin-lens estimate gives roughly 1:9; the true largest ratio could not be confirmed from an official source. Leica gives the length as approx. 46 / 58 mm depending on the integrated hood position; 46 mm (hood retracted) is used. Launch price: Leica's press release gives EUR 5,650 (black) / EUR 5,850 (silver); the USD 5,395 (black) figure is from DPReview/PetaPixel launch coverage (non-official). The smallest aperture f/16 is taken from the ePhotozine review (non-official).
famousFor: A classic fast 35mm for Leica M rangefinders; the 2022 redesign kept the compact size but added 11 aperture blades for smoother bokeh and closer 40 cm focusing, and reviewers rate it among the sharpest 35mm lenses Leica has made.
strengths: Very sharp across the aperture range, even wide open
Compact and light (about 320 g) for an f/1.4 lens
Close focus down to 40 cm, unusual for an M lens
Pleasant focus transition and rounder bokeh from 11 blades
weaknesses: Very expensive
Manual rangefinder focusing at f/1.4 takes practice; the 70-40 cm range needs live view or an EVF
Some vignetting wide open
bestFor: Street photography and reportage in low light
Everyday travel and documentary photography with a small kit
Close details at the table or on the street down to 40 cm

name: Leica Noctilux-M 50 f/0.95 ASPH.
notes: Order no. 11602 (black); silver (11667) and special editions such as the 2023 'Titan' version use the same optics. Leica lists 8 elements in 5 groups with two ground and polished aspherical surfaces/elements, glasses with anomalous partial dispersion and high-refractive-index glasses (their number is not published, so only the aspheres are itemised) and a floating element. Leica gives a length of 75.1 mm, 700 g, E60 filter thread, 1 m close focus and a largest reproduction ratio of 1:17 (stored as 0.059); the lens has a built-in extendable hood. The maximum diameter and the number of aperture blades were not found, so dimensionsMm and apertureBlades are null. Non-official values: announcement date (15 September 2008 at Photokina, availability February 2009) and the launch price of GBP 6,290 come from DPReview's launch article (a USD launch price was not verified); the smallest aperture f/16 appeared in spec listings (Leica / B&H) but not in a clearly official field.
famousFor: Leica's legendary f/0.95 standard lens, long billed as the world's fastest aspherical lens, sought after for its extremely shallow depth of field and distinctive 'Noctilux look' in available-light photography.
strengths: Extremely fast f/0.95 aperture for very low light
Distinctive, pleasant bokeh and razor-thin depth of field
Outstanding image quality when stopped down
Vignetting and distortion improved over the older Noctilux f/1
weaknesses: Heavy (700 g) and bulky for an M lens; it blocks part of the rangefinder view
Hard to focus accurately wide open; only focuses to 1 m
Strong vignetting until about f/4
bestFor: Street and concert photography in very dim light
Portraits isolating the subject with very shallow depth of field

notes: This is the current redesign announced by Leica on 13 April 2023 (order no. 11728 black, 11729 silver), which replaced the 2004-2023 version (11891/11892): 11 aperture blades instead of 9, close focus 45 cm instead of 70 cm via a double-cam focusing unit, and a round integrated lens hood. strengths: Compact and light for an f/1.4 standard lens
Close focus down to 45 cm, well below the traditional 70 cm M limit
Rounder out-of-focus highlights from the 11-blade diaphragm
Integrated, retractable lens hood

Manual rangefinder focusing at f/1.4 leaves little margin for error
bestFor: Head-and-shoulders and half-body portraits with soft backgrounds
Everyday travel photography with one small lens
Close-up details of food or objects down to 45 cm

New lens with little independent test data so far

name: Leica Vario-Elmarit-SL 24-70 f/2.8 ASPH.
notes: Order no. 11189. Announced on 6 May 2021 (Leica press release 2021; PetaPixel/DPReview). Leica lists 19 elements in 15 groups with three elements aspherical on both sides (six aspherical surfaces), nine elements of glass with anomalous partial dispersion, an 11-blade aperture and a closest focus of 18 cm at 24mm and 38 cm at 70mm measured from the sensor plane. The lens is made in Japan and shares its optical layout with Sigma's 24-70mm F2.8 DG DN Art; PetaPixel's review found differences suggesting it is not simply a rehoused Sigma. Non-official values: launch price USD 2,795, weight 856 g, dimensions approx. 88 x 123 mm and the 82 mm filter thread come from PetaPixel/DPReview launch coverage; the smallest aperture f/22, 0.34x maximum magnification (at the long end), the stepping-motor AF with a single-element internal focus group and the lack of optical stabilisation come from reviews (ePhotozine, PetaPixel, Digital Camera World). Whether the barrel extends when zooming was not confirmed, so zoomMechanism is omitted.
famousFor: A constant-f/2.8 standard zoom for the Leica SL system that shares its optical layout with Sigma's 24-70mm F2.8 DG DN Art, praised by reviewers for prime-like sharpness, near-zero distortion and very close focusing at 24mm.
strengths: Very sharp across the zoom range, with excellent edges from f/2.8
Distortion practically zero at all focal lengths in tests
Fast, quiet stepping-motor AF driving a single light focus element
Very close focus (18 cm at 24mm) and weather-sealed metal build
weaknesses: No optical image stabilisation
Large 82 mm filters
bestFor: Travel and everyday photography with one lens
